system_overview: This is a model-checking configuration module for the distributed replicated log specification. It extends the base specification and applies the finite monotonic technique by discarding the longest common prefix shared by all server logs, keeping the state space finite. Unlike the CRDT and replicated log model-checking modules, this approach does not require action composition but achieves finiteness through a view mapping.
actors_and_components: Same as the base distributed replicated log specification: a finite set of servers each maintaining their own append-only log. This module adds an assumption that the number of servers must be greater than one, since computing the longest common prefix with a single server would trivially shorten the log to empty.
state_variables: Inherits all state variables from the base distributed replicated log specification. No additional state variables are introduced.
initial_state: Same as the base specification: all servers start with empty logs.
actions: Inherits all actions from the base distributed replicated log specification (copy and extend) without modification. The finite state space is achieved through a view mapping rather than modified actions.
safety_properties: Inherits from the base specification: type correctness (logs are valid sequences), bounded lag (the absolute difference in log lengths between any two servers never exceeds the lag parameter).
liveness_properties: All extending: every server must always eventually strictly extend its log. In-sync: all servers should always eventually have identical logs. The model checker correctly finds a counterexample to the in-sync property, demonstrating that partial copying prevents guaranteed synchronization. However, the view-based approach may prevent TLC from correctly reconstructing counterexamples in general.
model_bounds: The server set is configured as three servers. The value set is configured as a single value. The lag parameter is set to three. The value set is assumed to be finite. The view mapping discards the longest common prefix shared by all server logs, reducing each log to only its suffix beyond the common prefix. Deadlock checking is enabled.
additional_assumptions: The longest common prefix approach is an alternative to action composition for achieving finite state spaces. It works by defining a view that projects away the common prefix of all logs, so states that differ only by a common prefix are identified. The module assumes more than one server exists and that the value set is finite. The specification notes that the view approach can prevent TLC from correctly reconstructing counterexamples in some cases.
